chunks: And indeed, the gates of the heaven,
are not closed on that night for the voices of the believers,
their sound is like the buzzing of bees,
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am your Lord, and you are My servants. You have fulfilled My right, and it is incumbent upon Me to answer you.'
So He removes [their sins] on that night for whom He wills to have his sins removed, and forgives whom He wills to be forgiven.

key_terms.تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ: That night (referring to the eve of Arafah)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the gates of heaven and the sins of believers on the night of Arafah?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Saduq highlights the unique status of the Eve of Arafah as a night of divine obligation rather than mere mercy, where Allah’s response to the pilgrims' collective supplication is compelled by their fulfillment of His right. The metaphor of the 'buzzing of bees' signifies the harmonious, pervasive nature of their voices, which remain unblocked by the heavens, ensuring that sins are expiated for those whom Allah wills.
